rated_messages.input_message: If you usually smoke while you talk on the phone, keep a pen and paper nearby to occupy your hands with doodling rather than smoking.
You cant always control when you will see other people smoking. But you can control how you respond to your urge when you do.
Think about times in the past when you have let urges pass during a stressful moment, and notice what helped make that moment easier.
Instead of smoking, take 10 deep, slow breaths and count them. Pay attention to what your breathing feels like. If you lose count, that's okay, just start over at 1 until you get to 10.
What inspires you most to quit smoking? Are you willing to let this urge pass without smoking for that reason?
Crumple a piece of paper into a ball and imagine it is your urge. Toss the "urge" into the garbage or against the wall. By doing this, you are letting go of your urges.
Instead of smoking, write a quick note to yourself explaining why ditching cigs is important to you. Carry it with you and read it when you feel like lighting up.
Setting small goals when you feel unmotivated is best. Maybe a small goal for now is to breathe deeply for the next 3 minutes instead of smoking.
Just because other people are smoking, doesn't mean you have to. Practice allowing this urge to be present for 5 minutes. When it passes, give yourself credit.
If you're stuck at home and physical activity doesn't interest you, try gaming, needlework, drawing, or journaling.
